title: Slow BTC/ETH time-series trend with scale-down-only volatility control (daily, long/cash)

mechanism.data: daily settlement price = Binance 1h spot close at 00:00 UTC of each date, aggregated locally from the collected monthly zips
mechanism.signal: sign(Close(D)/Close(D-120) - 1) per asset; long when positive, cash otherwise
mechanism.sizing: equal-weight across active assets (weights sum to <= 1); volatility overlay multiplies exposure by min(1, 0.50 / portfolio_vol) where portfolio_vol is the weighted average of 20-day realized vol (365-annualized). Scale-down-only: exposure is never levered above equal-weight
mechanism.execution: position decided with data through Close(D) earns the return over day D (Close(D) -> Close(D+1)); no leverage, no shorting
mechanism.costs: 12 bps one-way on |delta weight| each day (contract default); stress at 24 bps
mechanism.benchmark: equal-weight BTC/ETH buy-and-hold charged 12 bps at inception; cash as secondary baseline

notes: 534 fewer hourly bars than the ideal grid (0.035%); midsample gaps, all away from midnight stamps; no midnight settlement price missing
19 monthly files (2025-01 onward) use microsecond epochs; normalizing arithmetic verified against 53 ms-unit files
hour-grid repair: floor epoch to hour; 7,739 duplicate stamps in the raw concat via overlap of adjacent definitions; resolved, final hourly panel has zero duplicates and zero missing midnights

parameters.selection_rule: highest development net Sharpe at 1x costs

signal_timing.formation: daily at 00:00 UTC using Close(D) (= midnight price of D; the previous 23:00 bar's close)
signal_timing.returns: strategy_return(D) = pos(D) * (Close(D+1)/Close(D) - 1) for the day D span, minus costs
signal_timing.next_day_execution: positions established at the settlement price used in the signal timestamp; no same-tick data enters the signal
signal_timing.lag_guarantee: momentum uses Close(D) and Close(D-120); vol uses daily returns completing at Close(D); both known at formation

development_excess_vs_benchmark.note: dev excess is negative: the strategy's dev Sharpe edge vs buy-and-hold comes from volatility reduction, not extra return

edge_before_overlay.dev: raw trend Sharpe 1.2382 vs benchmark 1.0323 with annret 0.7551 vs 0.7270 and maxDD -0.566 vs -0.763: raw trend has the risk-adjusted edge
edge_before_overlay.validation: raw trend Sharpe 1.6072 vs benchmark 1.3563 with annret 0.7422 vs 0.7591: edge persists one year out

first_falsification_gate.definition: pre-registered before any 2024 observation: (a) validation net Sharpe > 0 and > named benchmark net Sharpe; AND (b) cumulative validation excess return at 2x costs >= 0; OR risk-overlay route: (a) plus lower validation maxDD at comparable return (within 5 percentage points of benchmark annret)
result_detail: (b) FAIL: cumulative excess -0.1287 at 1x and -0.1482 at 2x costs
risk-overlay route FAIL: maxDD -0.211 vs -0.355 (lower, good) but return 0.652/0.676 vs 0.759 annret is not comparable (7.7-10.7 pp shortfall, > 5 pp tolerance)

leakage_checks: signal inputs: Close(D) and Close(D-120) both observed at formation time; daily vol uses returns completing at Close(D): all lag-free
run.py fails closed when --end > 2024-12-31 unless QUANT_HOLDOUT_UNLOCK=1; flag never set during this work; selection and parameters independent of the flag
data manifest sha256 verified before every run

embargo discipline: no 2025+ observation was loaded into any selection or validation computation; the scratch parquet stores 2025-2026 timestamps only because aggregation was run once over the full collected archive; all masks cut at 2024-12-31 returns and no embargoed metric was computed or reported

windows: dev returns labeled 2020-08-03..2023-12-31 (1127 obs, warmup 120 trading days); validation 2024-01-01..2024-12-31 (366 obs); last validation return uses only the 2025-01-01 00:00 price, the first necessarily-required post-2024 print equal to validation-end return realization
survivorship/universe: fixed two-asset universe declared ex ante; no asset added or removed after seeing results
risks: single-asset concentrated crypto beta: buy-and-hold itself returned +83% in validation, so a long/cash trend overlay rides a rising market; excess-return falsification does not invalidate risk-adjusted merit
selection margin between top two dev variants is thin (1.3447 vs 1.3388): L60_V60 could have been chosen with materially similar results
dev excess return negative on all six variants vs buy-and-hold: the family's edge is volatility-reduction, fragile to the benchmark definition chosen by contract
scale-down-only overlay coupled with long/cash trend produces average exposure ~0.49-0.63: results are lever-agnostic but sensitive to target vol level (not tuned: fixed 50% by design)

midnight settlement convention vs close-auction alternatives shifts daily returns by ~0.2-6 bps/bars (mean 51.7 bps BTC per-book difference at 00:00 prints); robustness to this choice not separately tested within budget
two-asset panel with 19 missing hourly bars: negligible, but trend on stale prints during outages can flip signals
next_experiment: Since raw trend (no overlay) carried the entire edge and the overlay fails the contract's cumulative-excess requirement, the falsified family still motivates a follow-up: test whether raw 120d trend ON A RISK-ADJUSTED BASIS with explicit drawdown targeting (not scale-down-only) can convert vol reduction into benchmark-excess return in validation; otherwise the family should be shelved rather than re-tried with more lookbacks (trial budget discipline).
